Task 2: High Dimensionality Multi-Variate Anomaly Detection (HPE) With high dimensionality multi-variate anomaly detection, we intend to develop multi-variate anomaly detection models that span multiple and different systems, i.e., models that cover IT systems, CDUs, and cooling racks in a given E-Cell. NREL Deliverables: • NREL to provide HPE with the data necessary to support the HPE deliverables for this task. o Assure necessary time-series metrics are available as streams. (See list in Task 1.) HPE Deliverables: • Develop and deploy multi-variate anomaly detection models across systems of different types. Given the complexity of this task, we will limit the effort to a single E-Cell. So, for a given E-Cell, the multi-variate anomaly detection will be across a small number of CPU nodes, GPU nodes, switches, the single supporting CDU, and the two supporting Cooling Racks. • All multi-variate anomaly detection models to be correlated to the E-Cell’s power consumption. • Investigation of root-cause analysis. At a minimum, a literature review will be conducted to help HPE lay the groundwork for future root-cause analysis. Task 3: MLOps - Model Monitoring, Re-Training, and Re-Deployment (HPE) There are frequent changes in the data center, e.g., when a rack is taken out of service or brought into service, and these changes affect the data that the anomaly detection models are analyzing. The univariate and multi-variate models will need to be continuously trained using the latest data – model training, testing, and re-deployment are key parts of MLOps. Model performance metrics are the key inputs for detecting concept drift and triggering model re-training or model retirement. When concept drift is detected, model re-training is triggered. This will probably be the case for 100% of multi-variate models, deep learning-based, and some ML-based models. NREL Deliverables: • NREL to provide feedback on the deployment of model re-training and re-deployment. • NREL to work with HPE to propose models of anomalies and example anomalies to be subsequently analyzed. 13 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. HPE Deliverables: • Build ML training, validation, and testing pipelines for the anomaly detection models. • Investigate, develop, and deploy models to detect concept drift, and potentially identify the cause of the drift (e.g., via change point detection), and adjust model parameters after a certain time delay that is required to collect enough data. • Implement regular model re-training and re-deployment o Models will be re-trained and re-deployed when concept drift is detected. o Model re-training and re-deployment on a daily/weekly/monthly basis will be investigated in order to determine the most suitable period for model re-training. • Investigate, develop and deploy minimal capability to monitor model performance.
